scope.counting_policy: Document-page inventory, not a symbol/method count or compatibility score. API: each canonical documented feature/namespace/sub-API page counts once; st.column_config entry and its 21 dedicated column type pages are separate pages. Methods, parameters and state/return interfaces rendered within a page are subcapability links, not additional page entries. API group landings do not count as features. Concepts: only 21 selected behavior pages, not all concepts/tutorials. Redirect aliases and repeated cross-category links count once. Explicit does-not-exist warning pages are separately excluded, deprecated documented definitions retained. This is a minimum reproducible catalogue, not a claim of exhaustive API/method coverage.

entries.rust_plan: Mirror the measured 1.66.1 wire: a bounded-ownership run loop in the rerun handler whose `st.rerun()` iteration finishes FINISHED_EARLY_FOR_RERUN (rerun) or FINISHED_SUCCESSFULLY (stop) and, for rerun, immediately starts the next run without a client BackMsg; element pushes and session-state writes after the call are suppressed.
entries.compatibility_scope: Journey-execution-v1 measured subset: the aborted run finishes status 2 with the server starting the next run on the same session and a fresh run id; cascade end state identical to the reference. Three documented cross-side differences are recorded in .codex/compatibility.md (pre-existing per-run main_block delta, fast-rerun live streaming of the pre-rerun element, populated ForwardMsg.hash on lifecycle frames).
limitations: An unguarded rerun loops forever exactly as upstream; no depth cap is imposed.
Same-tick upstream message coalescing is not replicated: elements written just before st.rerun() stream live (matching the upstream slow case).
st.quit does not exist in 1.66.1 and is not offered.

entries.rust_plan: Mirror the measured 1.66.1 wire: st.stop() ends the run at the call point, keeps earlier elements, suppresses every later element and session-state write, and still finishes FINISHED_SUCCESSFULLY.
entries.compatibility_scope: Journey-execution-v1 measured subset: the stopped run keeps its prefix, never emits the epilogue and finishes status 0; session-state writes after the call are suppressed. Three documented cross-side differences are recorded in .codex/compatibility.md.
limitations: Suppression covers element pushes and session-state writes; other side effects of later user code still run (Rust has no unwinding).
st.quit does not exist in 1.66.1 and is not offered.
